_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for SetpointSmoother, each with the reason. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the reason lives in the same file as the claim. A declared equivalence leaves the denominator, so each one is a claim that has to be answerable. Both survivors are in the SAME line -- the `lpfilter_c` argument list -- and each is answered by a DIFFERENT mutant of that same line that the sweep KILLED, which is what keeps these from being two restatements of one excuse.
cabf8c14: `LocalVar->restart ? 1 : 0` -> `restart ? 2 : 0`, the `reset` argument to `lpfilter_c`. Answerable from the CALLEE, which is unit #14's C++ and is on this tree: `translations/Filters/lpfilter.cpp:39` consumes the parameter exactly once, as `if ((iStatus == 0) || (reset != 0))`. It is a test against zero and nothing else -- `reset` is not stored, not compared to 1, not arithmetic -- so 2 and 1 select the same branch and the same six coefficient writes. MEASURED, not only argued, and the measurement that matters is that the mutated value is CONSTRUCTED: `evidence/SetpointSmoother/harness.restart-false-probe.json` forces the argument to 0 and fails 40 of 13550, so 40 cases have `restart` TRUE and carry that truth into the filter, and the mutant passes all 40 by handing them a 2. Had that probe failed 0, this survivor would have been a fact about the CORPUS -- `restart` never true -- and not an equivalence at all; that is the distinction, and it is why the probe was run before the declaration. The sweep's own `restart ? 1 : 1` mutant (reset forced to 1) is killed on 47 cases from the other side, so 87 of 13550 cases observe this argument. THE LIMIT OF THE CLAIM, STATED: it holds against the C++ LPFilter this program links. It would NOT be safe against the original Fortran, whose dummy is `LOGICAL(4)` -- 2 is not a valid representation of a Fortran logical, and gfortran is entitled to do anything with it. The shipped call path is C++ to C++, so the shipped program is the one the claim is about.
439ac905: `..., 0, 0.0)` -> `..., 0, 1.0)`, the `InitialValue` VALUE argument to `lpfilter_c`. Answerable from the callee and from its neighbour in the same call. `translations/Filters/lpfilter.cpp:34-35` reads `double InitialValue_ = InputSignal; if (has_InitialValue) InitialValue_ = InitialValue;` -- the value is read only under the flag. The reference passes no InitialValue at this site (`LPFilter(DelOmega, LocalVar%DT, CntrPar%F_SSCornerFreq, LocalVar%FP, LocalVar%iStatus, LocalVar%restart, objInst%instLPF)`, seven arguments, ControllerBlocks.f90:463), so VIT's PRESENT flag is the literal 0 and the value is dead. THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS THE ADJACENT MUTANT AND THE SWEEP KILLED IT: `..., 0, 0.0)` -> `..., 1, 0.0)` flips the FLAG and dies on 3835 of 13550 cases. So the argument pair reaches the callee, the callee reads the value when told to, and the only reason this mutant survives is that it is told not to. A dead-argument survivor whose flag mutant also survived would have proved nothing -- it would have said the whole pair was unobservable.
_not_declared: Nothing else survived, so this file has no near-misses to record. Worth naming anyway, because the reason it has none is the corpus and not the operator set: at the 5599-case corpus that preceded `harness/ranges.toml`'s `CntrPar_SS_Mode = { values = [0, 1, 2] }`, FOUR cases reached the arm every one of these mutants lives on (evidence/SetpointSmoother/harness.if-arm-deleted.5599.json). The 16 behavioural kills are kills against 4516 such cases, not against 4.
